macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: U.S. stocks mixed as oil surge and AI concerns pressure markets
items.summary: The Nasdaq rose 0.2% and the S&P 500 fell 0.2% in Friday trading after both indexes hit roughly one-month lows. Higher crude prices and doubts about AI-related spending continued to weigh on sentiment.[1]

items.title: Nasdaq plunges 2.6% as AI financing concerns trigger tech selloff
items.summary: In the previous session, the Nasdaq fell 2.6% and the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index dropped 6.72%, while the S&P 500 declined 1.22%. Meta’s heavy AI capital spending and negative free cash flow intensified concerns about the sustainability of the AI trade.[4]

items.title: Oil rises above $100 amid Middle East supply risks
items.summary: U.S. crude moved back above $100 a barrel and Brent reached a five-month high as attacks and escalating regional tensions raised concerns about disruptions to energy supplies.[1][3]

items.title: Markets expect the Federal Reserve to hold rates steady
items.summary: The Fed is widely expected to leave interest rates unchanged at its upcoming meeting, while investors focus on policymakers’ guidance and continue to price a substantial probability of a December rate increase.[1][2]

items.title: Western Digital beats earnings and revenue estimates
items.summary: Western Digital reported fiscal first-quarter 2027 earnings of $4.64 per share on $4.38 billion in revenue, exceeding estimates of $4.07 per share and $4.13 billion, although its shares were slightly lower premarket.[5]

items.title: Global markets prepare for Fed, Bank of Japan and megacap earnings
items.summary: Investors are bracing for the Fed and Bank of Japan decisions alongside earnings from Microsoft and Alphabet on October 28 and Amazon on October 29, making the coming week a major test for equities.[6]

items.title: Japan inflation strengthens expectations for possible BOJ tightening
items.summary: Japan’s core consumer inflation rose 2.1% year over year in September, supporting expectations that the Bank of Japan could tighten policy in December.[7]

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Bitcoin Slides Below $82,000 as Crypto Liquidations Top $1 Billion
items.summary: Bitcoin fell roughly 3%–4.5% to about $81,300–$82,000, while Ether, Solana and XRP also declined. Crypto-market liquidations reached approximately $1.19 billion in 24 hours, with Ether liquidations exceeding Bitcoin’s in absolute terms.

items.title: U.S. Spot Bitcoin ETFs Record $635 Million Outflow
items.summary: U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs saw approximately $635.5 million in net outflows, the largest single-day withdrawals reported since June. BlackRock’s IBIT and Fidelity’s FBTC accounted for the largest reported fund outflows.

items.title: Thailand Drafts Rules for Bitcoin and Ether ETFs
items.summary: Thailand’s securities regulator reportedly completed rules allowing Bitcoin and Ether ETFs to trade on the Stock Exchange of Thailand. The rules are scheduled to take effect on October 16, 2026.

items.title: Spain Tightens Crypto-ATM Identity Checks
items.summary: Spain approved rules requiring reliable identity verification for all crypto-ATM transactions. Operators will reportedly receive an 18-month transition period to implement enhanced electronic verification systems.

items.title: Singapore, Malaysia and Thailand Expand Regulated Stablecoin Pilot
items.summary: The three countries are expanding the BLOOM initiative to test cross-border payments using regulated stablecoins and tokenized bank deposits. Ripple, Visa and Mastercard are among the reported participants, with Ripple planning trade-payment tests using RLUSD on the XRP Ledger.

items.title: Chainlink Partners With LG CNS on Korean Digital-Asset Infrastructure
items.summary: Chainlink and LG Group technology arm LG CNS reportedly agreed to develop compliant digital-asset infrastructure for South Korea’s market.

items.title: Russia Proposes Regulated Trading of Bitcoin, Ether and USDT
items.summary: Russia’s central bank reportedly proposed permitting Bitcoin, Ether and USDT on regulated exchanges while limiting annual crypto purchases by non-qualified investors to 300,000 rubles per intermediary.

items.title: Switzerland Approves First Direct Bitcoin Retail Fund
items.summary: Switzerland’s financial regulator reportedly approved the country’s first exchange-traded retail fund investing directly in Bitcoin under the legal category for alternative investments.

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

items.title: OpenAI makes Decisions API generally available
items.summary: OpenAI released its low-latency Decisions API for production use, targeting bounded choices such as classification, routing, and structured-input decisions. Reported features include voice integration, prompt caching, regional processing, and JSON support.

items.title: NVIDIA launches Minerva AI-operations platform
items.summary: NVIDIA introduced Minerva, a platform that combines GPU, network, storage, scheduler, and AI-workload telemetry to help diagnose infrastructure problems through a topology-aware knowledge graph.

items.title: Hugging Face releases Carbon-X DNA model
items.summary: Hugging Face released Carbon-X, an Apache-2.0 open model designed to answer natural-language questions about DNA sequences and support DNA understanding and generation.

items.title: DeepSeek releases V4.1-Flash-1017
items.summary: DeepSeek released an updated model focused on coding and agent tasks, with claims of stronger performance than larger rivals and substantially lower per-task costs.

items.title: Inception Labs releases Mercury 3 diffusion model
items.summary: Inception Labs launched Mercury 3, a diffusion-based language model that claims performance comparable to leading competitors while running four to eight times faster.

items.title: Google Cloud introduces Agent Compute Engine
items.summary: Google Cloud announced a managed service that provides AI agents with hardware-isolated microVMs, persistent storage, and short-lived credentials injected outside the sandbox.

items.title: Microsoft and Hugging Face announce ThinkingBox-Training
items.summary: The organizations released a training approach that uses executable checks of an agent’s final database state as reinforcement-learning rewards, aiming to improve reliability on operational tasks.

items.title: MiniMax releases M3.1 Flash model weights
items.summary: MiniMax released weights for M3.1 Flash, a multimodal mixture-of-experts model reported to contain about 428 billion parameters, with approximately 23 billion active per token.

items.title: Apple Intelligence launches in mainland China
items.summary: Apple launched Apple Intelligence features in mainland China, including Live Translation, Writing Tools, and Clean Up, while initially excluding AI-enabled Siri features.

items.title: Meta proposes new share class to fund AI expansion
items.summary: Meta is issuing a new non-voting share class intended to support AI initiatives, acquisitions, and employee compensation, with trading expected to begin in 2027.

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

items.title: EA cuts 400 jobs and closes BioWare
items.summary: Electronic Arts is reducing its global workforce by about 3% and closing BioWare, the studio behind Mass Effect. Development of the next Mass Effect reportedly has been canceled, while EA is prioritizing Battlefield, Apex Legends, Iron Man, and Star Wars Jedi.

items.title: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 launches amid franchise concerns
items.summary: The latest Call of Duty installment is launching after Black Ops 7 reportedly underperformed relative to the series’ historical sales position. Its release comes weeks before the expected launch of Grand Theft Auto VI.

items.title: South Korea outlines expanded game-industry support
items.summary: South Korean officials called for stronger support for domestic game intellectual property, AAA development, indie studios, and AI-related talent training. The culture minister also endorsed efforts to integrate esports more formally into the sports system.

items.title: US video game market broadly stabilizes in September
items.summary: The US game market generated about $4.76 billion in September, only slightly below the same period last year, while hardware and accessory sales returned to year-over-year growth, according to Circana data.

items.title: EA reportedly revives Fight Night boxing series
items.summary: EA Sports has announced the return of the Fight Night boxing franchise under the working tagline “The Fight Is Never Over,” according to an industry-news roundup.

items.title: Control Resonant surpasses one million sales
items.summary: Remedy Entertainment’s Control Resonant reportedly passed one million units sold, marking a significant commercial milestone for the action game.
